title: Implement a Threat Response Automation (TRA) Service
description: The ProdSecure Orchestrator can currently detect security threats via its `scan_service` and monitor system state. However, responding to these threats is a manual process. This task involves implementing a new Threat Response Automation (TRA) service. This service will listen for threat events and automatically execute pre-configured actions, such as isolating a node or triggering an emergency backup. This is a multi-session task designed to simulate a feature development lifecycle, requiring the agent to build upon its work from previous sessions.

project_spec.name: ProdSecure Orchestrator
project_spec.description:
ProdSecure Orchestrator (Project ID: c_system_security_expert_028) is a high-throughput, MVVM-driven command-and-control suite that turns routine security chores—back-ups, scanning, monitoring, and automated deployments—into streamlined productivity workflows. Operators interact through a declarative dashboard (View) that surfaces real-time performance metrics, aggregated logs, and AI-assisted remediation steps, while a dynamic Model layer consolidates configuration state, threat intelligence, and topology metadata coming from service-mesh sidecars. The ViewModel exposes intent-based commands—backup, balance, scan, deploy—using the Command and Strategy patterns so power users can chain, schedule, and reuse complex security tasks as one-click “productivity macros.” 

Distinct from traditional system-security consoles, this project treats security operations as reusable building blocks that can be composed, version-controlled, and batch-executed just like productivity scripts. Event-driven pipelines push telemetry to observers that update dashboards, trigger alerts, or adjust load-balancers without human latency, letting security engineers focus on higher-value optimization instead of repetitive maintenance. The complete toolchain is designed for 95 modular source files, enabling granular ownership and continuous delivery while maintaining a clear MVVM separation of concerns.
dependencies: GLib/GObject (core object system & signal dispatch for MVVM bindings)
GTK4 (UI toolkit for the View layer; property bindings to GObjects)
libevent or libuv (event-driven IO underpinning Service Mesh sidecar communication)
OpenSSL (encryption, certificate handling for secure channels)
libcurl (HTTP/2 client for pulling remote configs and pushing metrics)
ZMQ or NATS C client (high-volume pub/sub telemetry bus)
Prometheus C client & StatsD exporter (performance metrics)
